subject: PrivDeploy: layered IaC + CI rollback playbook review
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com, j.senior@integrate.io
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrivDeploy: layered IaC + CI rollback playbook review

Team —

I put together a short draft that attempts to unify how we deploy private stacks for customers that want a VPC/on-prem footprint while keeping a deterministic rollback surface. The gist:

- Keep Terraform strictly for long-lived infra (VPC, BGP, metal + LVM volumes) and remote state.
- Use Helm for service manifests and overlay values per environment (staging -> preprod -> prod).
- Use Ansible for machine-level bootstrapping, package installs, and config templating that Helm can't handle on air-gapped nodes.
- CI promotes artifacts through three gates: canary (ephemeral namespace), staging (integration/canary traffic), prod. Each promotion creates a timestamped release tag and a revert tag automatically.

Key ask: review the attached playbook that defines a rollback matrix (what to revert first, state reconciliation order, and safe points for manual intervention). Two particular areas I want eyes on:

1) Terraform state recovery when a Helm release requires a tf-managed LB to be recreated — outlined in section 3 of the playbook.
2) Handling helm value flips that are backwards-incompatible (we propose a two-step deprecation flag that gives the service a 1-week grace period to accept the new contract).

Context: Acme is asking for formal preflight checks and a documented rollback for their SOC/audit team; they also run a bespoke storage backend that has tight RTO requirements.

Attached: priv-rollback-playbook.md, ci-pipeline-snippets.diff

Can you skim and call out any missing preflight assertions (e.g., TF import checks, live KV cache eviction steps, or Ansible idempotency gates)?

Thanks —
Logan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: layered IaC + CI rollback playbook review

Logan —

Great layout. Quick notes after a pass:

- Terraform: add a step to snapshot remote state to an immutable bucket before any tf apply that modifies networking (we should keep a copy outside of the primary S3/GCS backend to protect against accidental overwrite). Also include a forced-lock-owner check so the apply fails fast if the remote lock owner is stale.

- Helm: recommend using chart-operator style rollbacks where we keep the last 3 release manifests in the repo; tie the release name to the git commit hash so the pipeline can do a deterministic rollback via git-revision -> helm rollback.

- Ansible: ensure every play has an explicit --check step executed in CI against an ephemeral VM image; if a play fails the check we abort promotion. Emphasize idempotency for service users who may have manual changes on boxes (documented in the playbook).

Action items from me:
1) Add TF pre-snapshot + restore steps to section 2.
2) Add a small Helm manifest sanitizer that compares rendered templates against a policy (we can reuse the existing OPA bundle).

I'll open a PR against the playbook with these diffs by EOD.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer

From: ops@acme-corp.com <ops@acme-corp.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, vendor-ci@buildpipe.io
Date: 2027-04-12T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: layered IaC + CI rollback playbook review

Thanks for the draft,

A couple of things from Acme infra side:

- Our RTO for stateful services (DB, indexer) is 30 minutes. If Terraform recreation of storage volumes is part of a rollback, we need a documented restore-from-snapshot flow that includes storage-provider-runbook and a DBA checkpoint. Can you add a clear gate that refuses an automated rollback unless the snapshot count >= 2 and last snapshot age < 24h?

- Air-gapped nodes: Ansible will be the only thing touching packages. We need the playbook to explicitly call out binary artifact staging (where we push tarballs) and a signed-artifact verification step.

- CI: when a rollback is initiated from the pipeline, will it automatically open a PagerDuty incident? We prefer a manual confirmation step for anything that touches persistent volumes.

Attached our internal snapshot policy and a short note on storage snapshot lifecycles.

Regards,
Priya Sen
Ops Lead, Acme Cloud
ops@acme-corp.com

--
Attachment: acme-snapshot-policy.md
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme-corp.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, vendor-ci@buildpipe.io
Date: 2027-04-12T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: layered IaC + CI rollback playbook review

Folks —

Thanks for the quick feedback, Priya & Karthik. I pushed an updated draft that:

- Adds TF pre-snapshot to the apply workflow and the acceptance gate you requested (snapshot count and age).
- Marks any persistent-volume changes as manual-confirm-only from the pipeline and wires those to trigger a PagerDuty incident via our incident orchestration step (will not auto-roll back).
- Adds an Ansible artifact signing verification and an explicit --check run in the ephemeral VM phase.
- Adds a Helm rollback policy that maps git tags -> helm releases and keeps a 3-release manifest history.

Next steps / owners:
- Karthik: please review the tf snapshot + lock-owner wording in section 2 (owner: karthik).
- Monica: can you validate the Ansible idempotency checklist on our two air-gap test images and report results by Tue 04/14?
- Mina: please add the OPA helm-sanitizer to CI and confirm the policy bundle version (owner: mina).
- Acme: Priya, if that timeline works we'll schedule a dry-run for your staging cluster Wed 04/14 09:00-11:00 PT. Please confirm.

I'll attach the updated playbook in the PR (priv-rollback-playbook.md) and link the pipeline snippets for review. If we get sign-off after the dry-run we'll add the playbook to the formal runbook collection and hand it to your audit team.

Cheers —
Logan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com
